title: How Alaska became a key battleground in the fight for the Senate
summary: Alaska's Senate race between Republican Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola could decide which party controls the Senate. In their debate, Sullivan called for a quick end to the Iran conflict to bring down energy costs, while Peltola rejected allegations about how she treated staff. Lori Townsend of Alaska Public Media explains how soaring fuel and grocery prices, tariffs and fishing-industry worries are shaping how rural Alaskans vote.
focus: Shadow Lori Townsend's explanation of how fuel costs and tariffs are squeezing rural Alaska and its fishing businesses: a clear, reporter-style account with lots of cost vocabulary.
